parsed.summary: The file defines R_k(3) as the least n such that every k-colouring of the edges of K_n has a monochromatic triangle. It then states four results: R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞; an explicit lower bound R_k(3) ≥ ((1/(6e^{38})) k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every k ≥ 2; eventual bounds (1/3−ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε) k log k; and log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k). These match Theorem 1.1, its corollaries, and (4) in the paper, with an explicit constant in place of the paper's 'there exists c'. No real caveats: the sInf/junk-value concerns are harmless because Ramsey numbers are finite and every statement is either asymptotic or restricted to k ≥ 2.

glossary.plain: A k-colouring C of E(K_n) in which no colour class contains a triangle (each colour graph is 3-clique-free).
Every k-colouring of E(K_n) contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: Upward closed in n, so sInf gives the threshold.

glossary.plain: R_k(3): the least n with the arrow property (sInf, which would be 0 if the set were empty).
glossary.note: The set is nonempty for every k because Ramsey numbers are finite. k=0 gives a degenerate value (2), which is irrelevant to every target statement.

lean_claims.plain: For every integer k ≥ 2, ((1/(6e^{38})) · k^{1/3} / log k)^k ≤ R_k(3); and R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞.
For every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large k, (1/3 − ε) k log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1 + ε) k log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for every integer k ≥ 2.
